correctness.rationale: Every regular orientation is an Eulerian orientation of K_(2m+1). The prescribed-outdegree max-flow/Hall criterion applied to H=G-S gives extension of every chosen orientation on S iff 2|S∩δ(U)|≤|δ(U)| for every cut. The two-clique construction has cut slack (a-b)(a-b+1), nonnegative for integral a-b. Singleton cuts yield deg_S(v)≤m; two-vertex cuts force degree-m vertices to form a clique of size ≤m+1; degree sum bounds 2|S|≤2m², and equality forces K_(m+1)∪K_m on separate parts. Independent enumerator recomputed regular tournament projections and all supports for n=3,5 (maximum 1 and 4, with 3 and 10 maximizers) and corroborated the all-m proof. The general criterion and rigidity rely on the written argument, not finite cases.

value.rationale: Exact VC dimension, all equality supports, and exact multiplicities of an intrinsically natural orientation concept class: simultaneously realizable edge directions subject to balance. Its cut/b-matching bridge is reusable across Eulerian orientations, while the rigid balanced-clique maximizers are not an arbitrary small slice or mere restatement of Hakimi feasibility.
